page0.text:
Fifth period is about to end.
Tohsaka finished explaining things to me, so I ask her about Shinji since he's also from a family of mages.

page1.text: "Hey, Tohsaka. Did you know that Shinji's family...the Matou family is a family of mages?"

page2.text:
"Yes, I know.
But my father said that they've declined over the past few decades. I heard that they don't have a bloodline of mages now.
That's the truth. It's also why I was surprised to hear that Shinji became a Master."

page3.text:
Oh, so she did know.
Of course. She supervises this land, so she knows all the families with a mage history. She should know that Shinji's a Master—Wait, hold on...!!!

page4.text:
"Tohsaka! You knew that Shinji was a Master too!?"
"Haha. Sorry, I found out this morning too. It looks like I underestimated him. My assumption that Shinji couldn't be involved backfired."
Tohsaka says as if it's nothing.

page5.text:
However...
Something's off.
She was searching for the third Master at school, yet she doesn't seem to consider Shinji as a problem at all...?

page6.text:
"Tohsaka? Shinji is a Master, right?"
"Yes. But it shouldn't be a problem. Shinji himself doesn't have any magical energy, so it's not like he can do anything outrageous.
Our enemy is the Master hiding at school. Shinji doesn't have any presence as a Master, so he's not the one we're looking for."

page7.text:
...Mm? So does that mean there are actually four Masters at our school?
"I would think so. Well, I don't think Shinji would interfere, since I told him not to do anything."

page8.text:
...Another statement that bothers me.
Wait, first of all, how did Tohsaka find out that Shinji's a Master...?

page9.text:
"Tohsaka. Can you tell me more about what happened this morning?"
"Mm? There's nothing to talk much about since Shinji was the one who told me.
He asked me if I wanted to team up with him since he became a Master as well."

page10.text:
...
I'm starting to get a bad feeling about this, but I can't stop her now.

page11.text:
"So what happened after that?"
"Nothing happened. I declined, of course.
...But he was so persistent about it. So I let slip that I don't need him since I have you."
Tohsaka laughs, recalling it.

page12.text:
"..."
That must the reason why Shinji was acting so strange.
However...

page13.text:
"...So what are you going to do about Shinji? Are you going to let him be? He's the one who set up the Bounded Field around school, right?"
"...What?"

page14.text:
Tohsaka freezes.
...I knew it. She didn't notice that Shinji was the one who set up the Bounded Field...!

page15.text:
"You're wrong, Tohsaka. It's true that Shinji isn't a mage. But he set up that Bounded Field. I'm sure he has a Servant that excels in magecraft like Caster."
Tohsaka grows pale.

page16.text:
"Tohsaka. You didn't notice?"
"...No. I knew that the Bounded Field was something done by a Servant, but..."
She couldn't make the connection with Shinji?

page17.text:
...I recall how Tohsaka was acting until now.
I bet she was so worried about last night's incident that she couldn't think about Shinji.
This might be the biggest mistake she's made in her life.

page18.text:
"This is bad. Shinji might be—"
Tohsaka gets up instantly and glares at the exit.
At that instant...
The abnormality around this school openly reveals itself with perfect timing.

page19.text:
"The Bounded Field...!"
The sky is tinted red.
Stagnant, red air immediately begins suffocating everything within the school grounds.
It won't affect mages who can cycle magical energy through their body to ward off this effect, but normal people will pass out, and if enough time goes by, they'll die—

page21.text:
Red surrounds everything in the school.
The hallway, red as blood.
The air, red as blood.
Thick air sticks to my skin and creates the sense that this is all just one horrible dream.

page22.text:
"Khh..."
Disgust threatens to rip itself out through my lips.
Like coolant, I try to force reasonable, controlled thoughts through my confused and heated brain.

page23.text:
I break for the classroom closest to the stairs on the fourth floor.
"Oh...!"
Tohsaka stops for a second, hesitant to enter this disastrous scene.

page24.text:
"...Ugh..."
...I know how she feels.
I don't like it any more than she does.

page25.text:
"...They're still alive. It's not too late to save them."
I check the nearest student for their pulse and breathing.
...There's not a conscious person left in this classroom.
The students who were sitting in their seats and the teacher at the podium are all lying on the floor.

page26.text:
Most of the students are unconscious, limp, and their eyes are clouded over.
...The few others...
A small handful of students had more unusual reactions.

page27.text:
...Their skin is congealing.
As if scorched by cold flame, their skin is stripped of all vitality and shines in the eerie light like melted wax.

page28.text:
Tohsaka is breathless before this scene of disaster.
...
We have no time.
To get to the bottom of this as fast as possible, I...
